drhp.business: Established in 1986, Butterfly is a leading player in the Indian appliances industry and a well-recognised brand in South India, ranking among the top kitchen appliances manufacturers in the country. With plant consolidation completed, the next phase focuses on automation and capacity readiness, with production planning being aligned to support anticipated growth, including a planned expansion of pressure cooker capacity from around 12 Lakh units towards 18 Lakh units. risks.note: Rising costs of metals, plastics and electronic components pressure margins; elevated global commodity prices and a weakening rupee increased input costs during FY26 and led to gradual price increases in Q4.
risks.risk: Raw material and input cost volatility

risks.note: Influx of new domestic and international brands across price points is intensifying competition in the kitchen appliances category, increasing both price and innovation pressure.
Growing promotional intensity on online marketplaces and channel fragmentation are compressing margins and increasing revenue volatility as distribution shifts toward online/e-commerce.
risks.risk: Channel fragmentation and online promotional intensity

risks.note: Regulatory requirements such as energy labelling, safety and environmental norms, combined with supply-chain volatility, are increasing compliance costs and lead times.

A weakening rupee, geopolitical tensions and global trade uncertainty affect input costs and demand momentum; management flagged sustaining growth amid these dynamics as a key consideration, with Q4 FY26 demand notably volatile.

The Company discloses exposure to a variety of laws, regulations, positions and interpretations - including direct taxation matters - creating contingent legal and tax risk (Board's Report, 'Risk arising out of litigation, claims and uncertain tax positions').
risks.risk: Litigation, claims and uncertain tax positions

risks.note: The Board-approved Risk Management Policy itself identifies strategic, financial, credit, market, liquidity, security, property, legal and regulatory risk as elements the Company may face, indicating a wide risk surface actively overseen by the Risk Management Committee.
